title: Security FAQ refresh — intake from field (AEs/SEs) — raw questions + draft answers (needs Security/GRC review)
linked_artifacts: Fireflies: 2026-02-20 Aurora Financial SSO/audit logs review
body:
Purpose
- This is the raw intake doc for the Enterprise Security Enablement Kit refresh.
- Sources: AE/SE deal support, support tickets, and RFP/security review calls.
- Goal: capture the exact customer questions, which accounts asked them, and a proposed answer draft. Security/GRC will convert into approved FAQ/RFP language.

How to use
- Each item includes: (a) question as asked, (b) who/where it came from, (c) why they’re asking (what they’re really trying to de-risk), (d) suggested answer (NOT yet approved), and (e) review owner + confidence.
- Confidence key: GREEN = we’re confident and already have consistent language; YELLOW = likely true but needs precise wording/caveats; RED = do not answer without Security/GRC/Legal.

Important reminders (field)
- Please do NOT promise roadmap (“coming soon”) in RFPs. If a control is not supported, we need the exceptions language + escalation path.
- SOC 2 report and other evidence: must follow evidence request playbook (NDA + GRC triage). Don’t email reports directly.
- Data residency: be precise about what ‘residency’ means (processing region vs support access vs logging/telemetry). Avoid blanket “all data stays in-region” unless explicitly true for the deployment mode.

Top themes (what’s showing up repeatedly)
1) Data handling: retention/deletion, “training on customer data”, prompt/output logging
2) Audit logs: what events exist, export options, retention controls
3) Identity & access: SSO/SAML, SCIM, RBAC granularity, admin controls
4) Encryption & key management: at-rest/in-transit, BYOK/KMS, HSM, customer-managed keys (esp. Private)
5) Residency & regulated workloads: EU bank requirements, healthcare, pharma, on-prem constraints
6) Assurance: SOC 2, ISO language, pen test frequency, vuln mgmt, incident response SLAs
7) Vendor risk: subprocessors, DPA, breach notification, support access model

============================================================
INTAKE ITEMS (raw)
============================================================

1) “Do you train your models on our prompts/outputs? Do you use customer data to improve the service?”
- Accounts / where:
  - Acme Health (security review, 2025-11-05)
  - Summit Insurance (questionnaire + follow-up email)
  - Repeated via Support: SUP-28790
- Asked by: Security + privacy (CISO / DPO)
- Underlying concern: IP leakage, PHI/PII usage, regulatory constraints
- Suggested answer draft (YELLOW; needs approved definitions):
  - Redwood does not use customer prompts/outputs to train foundation models.
  - Customer content is processed to provide the service. Any service telemetry is minimized and handled per the data retention policy.
  - For troubleshooting, limited access controls apply and are auditable (confirm exact wording: “support access is logged + least privilege”).
  - If any optional logging features exist, they must be explicit/opt-in (CONFIRM by deployment mode).
- Notes/questions:
  - Confirm the precise definition we can use for “train” vs “fine-tune” vs “improve models”.
  - Confirm whether we store prompts by default in Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
- Review owner: Olga Petrov + Naomi Feldman
- Confidence: YELLOW

2) “What’s your default data retention for prompts, outputs, and embeddings? Can we set it to 0? How fast do you delete?”
- Accounts / where:
  - Nordbank (EU residency + retention constraints, RFP kickoff 2026-01-16)
  - Aurora Financial (SSO/audit logs + retention specifics, 2026-02-20)
  - Summit Insurance (questionnaire turnaround, 2025-12-13)
- Asked by: Security + compliance + procurement
- Underlying concern: reduce breach impact + comply with internal policies (often 30/60/90 days)
- Suggested answer draft (RED until we lock wording):
  - Provide deployment-mode-specific retention: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
  - Clarify what is retained where: request payloads, generated outputs, system logs, audit logs, metrics.
  - Confirm deletion behavior and timelines (e.g., “within X days”) and whether customer can request accelerated deletion.
  - Audit log retention is a separate control from prompt/output retention.
- Notes/questions:
  - We need one canonical table with “data type → default retention → configurable? → who can change → evidence”.
  - Avoid saying “we don’t store any data” unless Private truly supports that end-to-end.
- Review owner: Marcus Lin + Daniel Carter
- Confidence: RED

3) “Do you support EU data residency? Where is data processed and stored? Do you have EU regions?”
- Accounts / where:
  - Nordbank (hard requirement: EU processing)
  - EMEA inbound (Hannah Schmitt thread + multiple prospects)
- Asked by: Risk + IT architecture
- Underlying concern: Schrems II, regulator expectations, internal ‘no US processing’ rule
- Suggested answer draft (YELLOW; must avoid over-claiming):
  - Redwood can run workloads in specific regions depending on deployment mode and commercial terms.
  - For Private (VPC/on-prem), customer controls the region/environment; clarify shared responsibility.
  - For Hosted/Dedicated, confirm which regions are available today and what metadata/telemetry may be processed cross-region (if any).
  - Provide a precise definition: “data residency” = processing + storage location for customer content; exclude global control plane unless explicitly in-region.
- Notes/questions:
  - Need approved wording for: “support personnel access from outside region” and “subprocessor locations”.
  - Need an objection-handling snippet: “if you require EU-only, Redwood Private is the cleanest path.”
- Review owner: Lukas Meyer + Olga Petrov
- Confidence: YELLOW

4) “Can we deploy in our VPC or on-prem? What is the architecture and shared responsibility?”
- Accounts / where:
  - Helix Pharma (private/on-prem constraints)
  - Continental Telco (platform team; wants network isolation)
- Asked by: Infrastructure + security engineering
- Underlying concern: network boundaries, audit requirements, change control
- Suggested answer draft (YELLOW):
  - Redwood Private supports deployment in a customer VPC and may support on-prem options for regulated/air-gapped environments (confirm packaging + availability).
  - Clarify what Redwood operates vs what customer operates (control plane, model artifacts, logs, backups, monitoring).
  - Clarify identity integration options in Private.
- Notes/questions:
  - We need a “Private deployment security appendix” section for RFPs (SE request; see Slack).
- Review owner: Colin O’Donnell + Fatima Noor
- Confidence: YELLOW

5) “Is Redwood SOC 2 Type II? What’s the audit period? Can we get the report?”
- Accounts / where:
  - Acme Health (explicit request)
  - Aurora Financial (urgent escalation thread)
  - Multiple RFPs
- Asked by: Procurement + security
- Underlying concern: baseline assurance; shorten vendor risk review
- Suggested answer draft (GREEN but exact fields need to match current report):
  - Redwood maintains a SOC 2 Type II report; it can be shared under NDA via the evidence request process.
  - Provide the request steps and typical SLA.
  - Clarify what’s in-scope (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) and any carve-outs.
- Notes/questions:
  - Ensure we don’t quote audit dates in the field unless we keep them current (use “most recent report available upon request under NDA”).
- Review owner: Daniel Carter
- Confidence: GREEN

6) “Are you ISO 27001 certified?”
- Accounts / where:
  - Asked in multiple questionnaires; also internal Slack debate (#sales)
- Asked by: Compliance
- Underlying concern: their policy says ‘must be ISO’
- Suggested answer draft (RED until we finalize do/don’t say):
  - Do NOT claim certification unless true.
  - Provide “alignment” language only if approved by GRC, with a mapping approach.
  - Offer alternatives: SOC 2 report, security controls summary, customer audit support (as appropriate).
- Notes/questions:
  - Need a one-pager: “ISO 27001 alignment (not certified)” with exact approved phrasing.
- Review owner: Olga Petrov + Michael Grant
- Confidence: RED

7) “What encryption do you use in transit and at rest? What ciphers? What about backups?”
- Accounts / where:
  - Aurora Financial (deep dive)
  - Continental Telco (security addendum)
- Asked by: Security architecture
- Underlying concern: meet encryption policy; key ownership
- Suggested answer draft (YELLOW):
  - In transit: TLS (confirm versions) for API/console.
  - At rest: encryption for storage volumes, databases, and backups (confirm scope).
  - Provide key management boundaries by deployment mode.
- Notes/questions:
  - Avoid listing cipher suites unless Security has the exact current configuration. High-level is usually sufficient for questionnaires.
- Review owner: Marcus Lin + Kevin Osei
- Confidence: YELLOW

8) “Do you support customer-managed keys (BYOK)? Which KMS? HSM? Who can decrypt?”
- Accounts / where:
  - Aurora Financial (KMS question)
  - Nordbank (key ownership)
- Asked by: Security + risk
- Underlying concern: control keys; insider threat; compliance
- Suggested answer draft (RED until product specifics are verified):
  - Describe what we can support today per deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).
  - If BYOK is only available in certain tiers, say so and route to SE for scoping.
  - Clarify operational model: key rotation responsibility, access boundaries, audit logging of key usage (if any).
- Notes/questions:
  - Need a crisp diagram: “data flow + encryption boundaries” (Design ticket exists).
- Review owner: Naomi Feldman + Marcus Lin
- Confidence: RED

9) “SSO: Do you support SAML? Which IdPs? Can we enforce SSO? Do you support SCIM?”
- Accounts / where:
  - Aurora Financial (SSO/SCIM + enforcement)
  - Summit Insurance (questionnaire)
- Asked by: IT + security
- Underlying concern: centralized access control, provisioning/deprovisioning
- Suggested answer draft (GREEN/YELLOW):
  - Redwood Console supports SSO via SAML (confirm) with major IdPs.
  - SCIM support: confirm scope (users, groups) and whether it’s GA for all enterprise tiers.
  - Enforcement controls: confirm “SSO required” and any break-glass admin behavior.
- Notes/questions:
  - Need one standard paragraph for: SSO/SAML, SCIM, RBAC, and “API keys vs user auth”.
- Review owner: Hanae Suzuki + Markus Klein
- Confidence: YELLOW (until we confirm SCIM scope)

10) “RBAC: How granular are roles? Can we restrict by project/org? Are API keys scoped?”
- Accounts / where:
  - Continental Telco (platform team)
  - Aurora Financial
- Asked by: Platform security
- Underlying concern: least privilege, separation of duties
- Suggested answer draft (YELLOW):
  - Provide role model summary and whether it covers console + API.
  - Clarify permission boundaries for: model management, keys, billing, audit logs, retention settings.
- Notes/questions:
  - We need a sales-friendly RBAC summary that matches the actual policy bundle.
- Review owner: Hanae Suzuki + Colin O’Donnell
- Confidence: YELLOW

11) “Audit logs: Do you log admin actions and API events? What fields? Can we export to our SIEM?”
- Accounts / where:
  - Aurora Financial (explicit SIEM integration)
  - Summit Insurance
- Asked by: Security ops
- Underlying concern: detection/forensics; compliance requirement
- Suggested answer draft (YELLOW):
  - Provide event taxonomy (admin actions, auth changes, key creation, policy changes, etc.) and confirm whether inference requests are included or excluded.
  - Export: confirm available destinations (e.g., S3/SIEM) and current limitations.
  - Retention controls: confirm what’s configurable and what’s fixed.
- Notes/questions:
  - We need a single “audit log fields” list and a ‘no surprises’ limitations section.
- Review owner: Kevin Osei + Marcus Lin
- Confidence: YELLOW

12) “Do you have vulnerability management and pen testing? How often? Can you share results?”
- Accounts / where:
  - Helix Pharma (security expectations)
  - Multiple security questionnaires (pen test frequency)
- Asked by: AppSec
- Underlying concern: external assurance; patch SLAs
- Suggested answer draft (YELLOW/RED depending on evidence ask):
  - High-level: Redwood runs vulnerability scanning and periodic third-party penetration testing.
  - For results: summary may be shareable under NDA, but avoid committing to raw reports unless process allows.
  - Patch management: provide policy-level language (no hard SLAs unless approved).
- Notes/questions:
  - Need approved statement on pen-test cadence that Security is comfortable with.
- Review owner: Marcus Lin + Daniel Carter
- Confidence: YELLOW

13) “Incident response: breach notification timeline? Do you have 24/7 monitoring? Do you have an IR plan?”
- Accounts / where:
  - Helix Pharma procurement/legal sync (2026-02-03)
  - Continental Telco (security addendum)
- Asked by: Legal + security
- Underlying concern: contractual obligations and response readiness
- Suggested answer draft (RED; Legal + Security):
  - Confirm Redwood has an incident response program.
  - Breach notification timelines are contractual; provide standard DPA language only.
  - Monitoring/on-call: give high-level statement; avoid “24/7 SOC” unless true.
- Notes/questions:
  - Align with Legal on standard contract positions; do not improvise in RFP.
- Review owner: Michael Grant + Marcus Lin
- Confidence: RED

14) “Subprocessors: who are they? Where is the list? How do you notify customers of changes?”
- Accounts / where:
  - Helix Pharma procurement thread
  - Nordbank
- Asked by: Vendor risk
- Underlying concern: data access by third parties; cross-border processing
- Suggested answer draft (GREEN/YELLOW):
  - Provide canonical location for subprocessor list and the notification mechanism.
  - Clarify subprocessors vs infrastructure providers.
- Notes/questions:
  - Ensure the link is always current; avoid pasting an outdated list into emails.
- Review owner: Olga Petrov
- Confidence: YELLOW

15) “HIPAA/BAA: can you sign a BAA? Are you HIPAA compliant?”
- Accounts / where:
  - Acme Health (healthcare)
- Asked by: Compliance + legal
- Underlying concern: PHI processing
- Suggested answer draft (RED; Legal + Security + commercial):
  - Do not claim HIPAA compliance unless formal position exists.
  - If BAA is available only under certain conditions, specify gating criteria and route to Legal/Sales leadership.
- Notes/questions:
  - Need a standard snippet: “we can discuss a BAA in enterprise agreements” vs “not offered” (TBD).
- Review owner: Michael Grant + Sofia Mendes + Olga Petrov
- Confidence: RED

16) “Can we disable vendor support access? How do Redwood employees access customer environments? Is it logged?”
- Accounts / where:
  - Nordbank
  - Continental Telco
- Asked by: Security + IT
- Underlying concern: insider threat, sovereignty
- Suggested answer draft (YELLOW):
  - Describe support access model: least privilege, time-bound access, approvals, and auditability (confirm exact controls).
  - For Private: customer-controlled access boundaries.
- Notes/questions:
  - We need an explicit “support access” section in the FAQ.
- Review owner: Marcus Lin + Colin O’Donnell
- Confidence: YELLOW

17) “Do you provide data deletion certificates / attestation? How do we verify deletion?”
- Accounts / where:
  - Summit Insurance
  - Nordbank
- Asked by: Compliance
- Underlying concern: evidence for internal audits
- Suggested answer draft (RED):
  - Provide policy statement; if we can provide an attestation letter, it should be through GRC process.
  - Avoid committing to “certificates” unless we have a template.
- Notes/questions:
  - Need GRC to confirm what we can provide (and SLA).
- Review owner: Daniel Carter + Olga Petrov
- Confidence: RED

18) “Business continuity / disaster recovery: RTO/RPO? Multi-region? Backups?”
- Accounts / where:
  - Continental Telco RFP
  - Aurora Financial
- Asked by: Risk management
- Underlying concern: operational resilience
- Suggested answer draft (RED/YELLOW):
  - Provide high-level resilience approach; only share RTO/RPO if approved and accurate.
  - Deployment-mode differences likely significant.
- Notes/questions:
  - Confirm whether we have standard RTO/RPO ranges we can share.
- Review owner: Marcus Lin + Daniel Carter
- Confidence: RED

19) “Logging content: are prompts/outputs included in logs (app logs, system logs, audit logs)?”
- Accounts / where:
  - Acme Health
  - Aurora Financial
- Asked by: Security + privacy
- Underlying concern: accidental retention of sensitive content
- Suggested answer draft (RED; must be precise):
  - Distinguish: operational logs vs audit logs vs optional request logging.
  - Confirm whether content is redacted or excluded.
- Notes/questions:
  - This is one of the easiest places to overstate. We need exact product behavior per mode.
- Review owner: Naomi Feldman + Kevin Osei
- Confidence: RED

20) “Do you support customer-managed networking (PrivateLink, IP allowlists), and do you offer static egress IPs?”
- Accounts / where:
  - Continental Telco
  - Aurora Financial
- Asked by: Network/security
- Underlying concern: secure connectivity, reduce attack surface
- Suggested answer draft (YELLOW):
  - Provide current controls by deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).
  - If any item is ‘possible via custom’, clarify it is scoping-dependent and not default product.
- Notes/questions:
  - SEs need a clean snippet that avoids ‘yes’ without caveats.
- Review owner: Colin O’Donnell + Markus Klein
- Confidence: YELLOW

============================================================
Open questions to resolve (for Security/GRC)
- Define customer content handling for each mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private): what is stored, where, for how long, and who can access.
- Confirm exact audit logging coverage and export destinations + current limitations.
- Confirm identity integrations: SAML enforcement, SCIM scope, RBAC granularity, and API key scoping.
- Confirm key management options and how we describe KMS/HSM without implying capabilities not available.
- Confirm approved statements for: ISO 27001 (cert vs alignment), pen test cadence, and vulnerability management.
- Confirm legal positions for: breach notification timeline language, BAA/HIPAA, deletion attestations, BC/DR metrics.

Field notes (common pitfalls we’ve seen)
- “We don’t store prompts” → almost always needs caveats. Customers interpret this as ‘no content anywhere including logs/backups’.
- “EU residency” → customers interpret as ‘no US access, no US subprocessors, no global control plane.’ We must define scope explicitly.
- “SOC 2 covers everything” → it may not cover Private/on-prem the same way; avoid oversimplification.

Next steps
- Stephanie + Talia to convert this intake into: (1) a prioritized FAQ draft outline, (2) a claims matrix row per item, and (3) a standard RFP response block per theme.
- Assign owners for final language approvals per domain (Security Eng, GRC, Legal).
- Once approved: publish to Confluence enablement index and update HubSpot snippets/templates.

Last updated
- 2026-02-21 (added Aurora Financial and Helix Pharma items; marked retention + content-logging as RED pending canonical wording).
